messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] kv-pageout-spike | cluster: us-central-1b | metric: pageout_rate | value: 11.2/s | threshold: 3.0/s
olivia: seeing elevated latencies + NCCL timeouts reported by runtime. Paging alarms across multiple Dedicated pools.
mike: i'm taking triage. Which pool and which shard(s)?
lina: CS reports errors from two enterprise tenants around 11:05 UTC — API timeouts and some 5xxs. Ticket IDs 5542, 5543.
sam: quick skim of metrics: kv-tensor-7 resident_bytes jumped, and continuous-batcher backlog exploded. suspect new partitioner deploy (2026-03-15T09:58) changed shard assignments.
incident-bot: recent-deploy: partitioner-v2 promoted at 09:58 UTC in us-central-1b
rachel: logs show NCCL handshakes failing during TP syncs: "NCCL ERROR: unhandled cuda driver error" + repeated evictions.
aaron: paste of tail logs:
```
[11:03:49] kv-tensor-7 evict_count=5020 resident=104GB
[11:04:01] continuous_batcher backlog_tokens=1.1M max_batch_tokens=256000
[11:04:04] nccl: NCCL WARN Call to cudaGetDevice returned error
```
mike: we need fast, low-risk mitigations. Options: 1) roll back partitioner-v2 in affected AZ, 2) toggle continuous batching off for the pool, 3) trigger an immediate reshard (risky). Thoughts?
sam: toggle batching off first. Reshard mid-NCCL-errors could make things worse.
olivia: agree. Disable continuous batching for affected Dedicated pools and scale up pod memory temporarily if we can. Also reduce max_batch_tokens to cut accumulation.
incident-bot: action_recorded: disable_continuous_batching by sam at 11:09 UTC
lin a: (typo) lina: I'll notify the two affected customers and offer a temporary capacity bump.
sam: applying flags: `runtime.continuous_batching.enabled=false` and `runtime.max_batch_tokens=128000` to pool us-central-1b now.
incident-bot: flag_update: runtime.max_batch_tokens=128000 applied at 11:11 UTC
mike: initiating rollback of partitioner-v2 in us-central-1b canary ring. Routing to previous partitioner.
rachel: watch KV distribution after rollback. pulling resident set sizes across shards.
aaron: metrics during mitigation:
```
11:12:10 batching.queue_len: 1.0 -> 0.3
11:13:22 pageout_rate: 11.2/s -> 2.4/s
11:13:55 nccl_retry_count: 520 -> 14\`
```
sanjay: nice. That looks like the most impactful combo. We should not reshard while NCCL errors are present.
mike: rollback completed in AZ at 11:15 UTC. partitioner reverted to v1 affinity mapping.
rachel: post-rollback resident_bytes across kv-tensor shards:
```
shard-0: 50GB
shard-1: 49GB
shard-2: 51GB
shard-3: 48GB
shard-4: 47GB
```
olivia: customer impact summary (11:03-11:15 UTC): two enterprise tenants experienced elevated p95 latencies and intermittent 504s. We provided a temporary capacity bump to tenant #5542 for 1 hour. Estimated SLA impact: ~0.6% error budget burn for those tenants. Lina to confirm final list.
lina: confirmed tenants: global-logistics, shopwise. Both acknowledged and accepted temporary bump. CS to follow up.
aaron: root cause hypothesis: partitioner-v2 changed hash/replica placement semantics which created a hotspot on kv-tensor-7. With continuous batching unchanged, that shard's resident set grew beyond expected, causing evictions/paging and provoking NCCL handshake retries on TP boundaries.
sanjay: follow-ups and mitigations: 1) add pre-rollout distribution checker that computes expected per-shard resident skew and blocks if skew > 15% (owner: sam, ETA: 48h); 2) add runtime guard so continuous batching auto-throttles when per-shard resident > threshold (owner: sam, ETA: 72h); 3) extend integration tests to include partitioner rollouts under synthetic KV distributions (owner: rachel, ETA: 24h); 4) runbook update for "NCCL errors + paging" scenario (owner: mike, ETA: 3 days).
olivia: assigning on-call follow-ups: @sam implement guard; @rachel test coverage; @mike runbook; @lina customer comms. I'll take monitoring tweaks.
incident-bot: incident_severity: SEV-2 set at 11:20 UTC. timeline: https://internal/redwood/incidents/1976001234
mike: quick runbook note: if you see NCCL timeouts + pageouts, first disable continuous batching on the pool before attempting reshard or partitioner changes. Saves a lot of traffic churn.
aaron: i'll draft the postmortem and include the deploy diff and KV metrics. Will also attach customer timelines.
olivia: on-call handoff: @rachel will lead postmortem writeup and follow-ups after this shift. Thanks for the quick response team. :thumbsup:
rachel: taking lead. I'll coordinate with engineering and CS for the full postmortem + timeline. Closing active mitigation thread but will keep channel updated with follow-ups.
